security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU TCG emulates mseccfg.MML bit 0→1 transition but does not re-evaluate all TLB-cached PMP access decisions (e.g., cached code-translation blocks or cached page protections), guest M-mode code could execute from regions previously allowed but now denied under the Smepmp MML truth table (case c of MML spec: M-mode execution requires explicit M-mode-only or locked-shared-region rule). Similarly, if mseccfg.MMWP transitions 0→1 without flushing cached PMP bypass for M-mode, cached TLB entries could grant M-mode access to regions that should now be denied. Conversely, RLB transitions that unlock locked PMP entries without TLB flush could leave stale denial caches.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mseccfg write handler does not tlb_flush on every sticky-bit change that alters PMP access semantics; OR pmp_hart_has_privs truth table incorrectly maps smepmp_operation codes to allowed_privs for M-mode vs S/U-mode; OR mseccfg_csr_write fails to enforce RLB lock-out when any pmpcfg.L is set in disabled (OFF) entries; OR pmpcfg_csr_write allows executable M-mode-only or locked-shared-region configurations when MML=1 and RLB=0 (spec clause 4b); OR mseccfg.MML/MMWP re-enabled after migration resume without TLB invalidation
security_spec.summary: QEMU must re-validate all cached PMP access decisions (TLB flush) on any mseccfg sticky-bit change (MML/MMWP/RLB) and must correctly implement the 32-entry Smepmp truth table in pmp_hart_has_privs, including the MML-mode-specific redefinition of pmpcfg.L semantics and RLB-gated lock bypass

findings.finding: mseccfg is only cleared on reset when ext_smepmp is true, but Zkr (USEED/SSEED bits [9:8]), Smmpm (PMM bits [33:32]), and Zicfilp (MLPE bit [10]) also store security-critical state in mseccfg. If any of these extensions are enabled without Smepmp, a warm reset leaves those fields at their previous values, violating norm:mseccfg_useed_sseed_rst ('must have defined reset values') and norm:mseccfg_mlpe_rst ('MLPE field is reset to 0').

spec_citations.excerpt: The MML, MMWP, and RLB fields of the mseccfg register are set to 0, unless the platform mandates a different reset value. [...] The USEED and SSEED fields of the mseccfg CSR must have defined reset values. The system must not allow them to be in an undefined state after reset. [...] If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, the mseccfg.MLPE field is reset to 0.

findings.finding: The MLPE bit handling `val |= (val & MSECCFG_MLPE)` is a no-op — OR'ing val with a masked subset of itself produces no change. This looks like a copy-paste error from the sticky-bit pattern on line 688 (`val |= (env->mseccfg & mask)`). If MLPE was intended to be a sticky (forward-only) bit per Zicfilp's 'forward CFI' semantics, this implementation fails to make it sticky — guest can clear MLPE at will. If MLPE is intentionally not sticky, this is dead code that confuses future maintainers.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Zicfilp extension adds the MLPE field in mseccfg. When MLPE field is 1, Zicfilp extension is enabled in M-mode. When the MLPE field is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in M-mode and the following rules apply: The hart does not update the ELP state; The LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.

findings.finding: Sticky-bit enforcement for MML, MMWP, and PMM is correctly implemented: `val |= (env->mseccfg & mask)` prevents clearing once set (line 688). TLB flush is correctly triggered when any sticky bit changes state (lines 689-690), re-evaluating all cached PMP access decisions per norm:mseccfg_mml_sticky and norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl. RLB lock-out is correctly enforced when any PMP entry has L=1 and current RLB=0 (lines 676-684), matching norm:mseccfg_rlb_op_warl ('when mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry, including disabled entries').

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), then mseccfg.RLB remains 0. [...] This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset.

findings.finding: The Smepmp enhanced PMP truth table implementation correctly maps all 16 smepmp_operation codes to allowed_privs for both M-mode and S/U-mode. M-mode checks (lines 445-475) correctly deny access for S/U-mode-only rules (ops 0-8 except shared regions 2,3), allow execute from locked M-mode-only and locked shared-code regions (ops 9-11,13), and enforce read/write/execute per spec. S/U-mode checks (lines 476-509) correctly deny access for M-mode-only rules (ops 8-9,12-14), allow execute from S/U-mode-only regions (ops 1,10,11), and enforce shared-region semantics. All 16 encodings match the normative truth table in norm:mml_truth_table.

spec_citations.excerpt: The physical memory protection rules when mseccfg.MML is set to 1 are summarized in the truth table below. [16-row table mapping L,R,W,X to M Mode and S/U Mode permissions]

findings.finding: The X-restrict enforcement correctly rejects pmpcfg writes that would create executable M-mode-only or locked shared-region rules when MML=1 and RLB=0. Invalid operations (9,10,11,13) correspond to: op9=locked-execute-only, op10=locked-shared-code-exec-only, op11=locked-shared-code-RX, op13=locked-read-execute. When MML=0 or RLB=1, the restriction is correctly bypassed, allowing boot firmware to configure PMP entries before locking them. Matches norm:mseccfg_mml_X_restrict.

spec_citations.excerpt: Adding a rule with executable privileges that either is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is not possible and such pmpcfg writes are ignored, leaving pmpcfg unchanged. This restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.

findings.finding: Default PMP policy correctly implements: (1) MMWP=1 denies all modes including M-mode (norm:mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl — 'changes the default PMP policy for M-mode to denied instead of ignored'), (2) MML=1 allows M-mode R/W only when not executing, denies all other modes (norm:mseccfg_mml_exec_code — 'Executing code with Machine mode privileges is only possible from memory regions with a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule'), (3) defaults to M-mode full access when no special flags.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mseccfg.MMWP (Machine-Mode Allowlist Policy) [...] changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don't have a matching PMP rule. [...] When set it changes the default PMP policy for M-mode [...] to denied instead of ignored.

findings.finding: PMP entry read-only enforcement correctly depends on both the LOCK bit being set AND mseccfg.RLB being clear. When RLB=1, locked entries become writable (Rule Locking Bypass), matching norm:mseccfg_rlb_op_warl: 'When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules may be removed or modified.'

spec_citations.excerpt: When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules may be removed or modified and locked PMP rules may be edited. When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0.

findings.finding: mseccfg migration is correctly implemented as a conditional subsection, gated by mseccfg_needed() which returns true when any extension that uses mseccfg fields is enabled (ext_smepmp, ext_zkr, ext_smmpm, ext_zicfilp). The subsection correctly saves/restores env.mseccfg as a target_ulong. Registered under vmstate_riscv_cpu subsections array (line 521).

CSR existence predicate correctly gates mseccfg CSR on any of the three extensions that define fields in it: ext_smepmp (MML/MMWP/RLB), ext_zkr (USEED/SSEED), ext_smmpm (PMM). Matches norm:mseccfg_presence: 'It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented.' Note: Zicfilp (MLPE field) is not listed in have_mseccfg, but Zicfilp CSR validation requires ext_zicsr which implies CSR infrastructure, and mseccfg would exist through another extension or be unavailable — this is a design gap per PR review feedback but not a security vulnerability.

spec_citations.excerpt: It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.

findings.finding: pmpcfg_csr_write correctly iterates over all pmpcfg entries in the register, delegates to pmp_write_cfg for per-entry validation (read-only check, Smepmp invalid-cfg check, MTMATCH handling), and flushes TLB + updates rule count when any entry was modified. This ensures cached TLB entries are invalidated when PMP configuration changes, preventing stale permission caching.

pmpaddr_csr_write correctly enforces TOR lock propagation: when writing pmpaddr[i] and pmpaddr[i+1] uses TOR matching and is locked+RLB=0, the write is rejected. When not read-only, the address register is updated, pmp_update_rule_addr recalculates the cached SA/EA range, and tlb_flush invalidates cached TLB entries. The TOR lock check prevents bypassing locked PMP entries by shrinking the address range of a preceding TOR entry.

CSR dispatch wrapper correctly delegates to mseccfg_csr_write() in pmp.c, following the standard pattern for CSR handlers. The CSR table entry at line 6226-6227 correctly uses have_mseccfg predicate and min_priv_ver PRIV_VERSION_1_11_0.

riscv_cpu_post_load only recomputes env->xl after migration resume and does not perform TLB flush. While the current implementation reads mseccfg and pmp_state directly during address translation (no intermediate cached representation), if future optimizations add a cached 'effective PMP policy' derived from mseccfg bits, the lack of post-load TLB invalidation could cause the destination VM to use stale permissions computed from the source's pre-migration mseccfg state. Adding an explicit tlb_flush in post_load when mseccfg is non-zero would be a defense-in-depth measure.

KVM mseccfg synchronization is not implemented. The KVM CSR synchronization table (kvm_csr_cfgs) and reset function (kvm_riscv_reset_regs_csr) contain no references to mseccfg. This is consistent with KVM for RISC-V not yet implementing the Smepmp extension (kvm_multi_ext_cfgs does not include smepmp). When KVM adds Smepmp support, mseccfg synchronization must be added to kvm_cpu_riscv.c.
